statement: Genesis 1 and Enūma Eliš both begin from a watery primordial setting and move toward an ordered cosmos, while differing sharply in divine conflict, theology, and the mechanism of creation.

sources.author: Genesis
sources.access_note: Canonical text used only for the observable literary features stated here.

sources.citation: Metropolitan Museum of Art, “Mesopotamian Creation Myths,” Heilbrunn Timeline of Art History.
sources.author: Metropolitan Museum of Art
sources.access_note: Summarizes Enūma Eliš's primordial waters, Marduk-Tiamat combat, and ordering of the cosmos.

does_not_demonstrate: Parallel motifs do not by themselves demonstrate direct literary borrowing.
The shared watery setting does not establish that Hebrew tehom is borrowed directly from the name Tiamat.
notes: This observation is intentionally separate from the disputed causal-engagement claim.
